I submitted my initial dispute on XX/XX/XXXX, along with a Federal Trade Commission ( FTC ) Identity Theft Report and additional documentation supporting my claim. Violations of the FCRA 1.Failure to Conduct a Reasonable Investigation ( 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) ( 1 ) ) Under the FCRA, credit reporting agencies are required to conduct a reasonable investigation upon receiving a dispute. Despite providing a comprehensive FTC Identity Theft Report and detailed supporting evidence, I have not received confirmation of any substantive investigation into the disputed items.

2.Failure to Notify Me of Investigation Results ( 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) ( 6 ) ) The FCRA mandates that consumers be notified of the results of an investigation within 30 days of submitting a dispute. To date, I have not received any such notification, nor have I been informed of the outcome of your review or the process by which my dispute was evaluated.

3.Failure to Block Inaccurate Information Promptly ( 15 U.S.C. 1681c-2 ) The FCRA requires credit reporting agencies to block information resulting from identity theft upon receipt of appropriate documentation, such as an FTC Identity Theft Report. This has not occurred in my case.

Precedent Cases Supporting My Position Your failure to comply with FCRA requirements is not only a violation of my rights but also exposes your agency to liability, as demonstrated in precedent cases : XXXX v. TransUnion Corp. ( XXXX ) : This case emphasized that credit reporting agencies have a duty to conduct reasonable investigations beyond relying on the data provided by furnishers. 

XXXX v. TransUnion LLC  ( XXXX ) : The Supreme Court upheld consumer rights in disputes related to credit reporting inaccuracies, reinforcing the accountability of credit bureaus under the FCRA. 

Requested Resolution To resolve this matter, I demand the following actions : 1.Conduct a reasonable and thorough reinvestigation of the disputed accounts and transactions associated with my identity theft.

2.Provide a detailed written summary of your investigation, including the steps taken and evidence reviewed.

3.Immediately block or remove all inaccurate information resulting from the identity theft.

If this matter is not resolved promptly, I will have no choice but to escalate my complaint by filing with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ), the Federal Trade Commission ( FTC ), and potentially pursuing legal remedies.

Legal Violations Committed by American Express and XXXX XXXX. Unlawful Reporting of an Authorized User Account ( FCRA Violations 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq. ) I was only an authorized user on this account, not the primary account holder.

XXXX. Unlawful Credit Reporting No Permissible Purpose FCRA 1681b requires that a consumer provide written authorization before a financial institution reports an account under their name. 
Since I never agreed to be personally liable for this account, American Express and XXXX have violated this law by reporting inaccurate information. 
XXXX. Failure to Conduct a Reasonable Investigation ( FCRA 1681s-2 ( b ) ) American Express has refused to provide : A signed contract proving I agreed to be liable for this account. 
Documentation proving I authorized this account to be reported under my credit. 
Evidence that I linked my business checking account to this credit card. 
Since they have failed to produce this evidence, they must remove the account immediately.

Reporting conflicting or missing data ( e.g., different monthly payments, missing dates, varying delinquency histories ) violates this requirement.

15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) ( 5 ) Correction or Deletion If the investigation finds the disputed information to be inaccurate, incomplete, or unverifiable, it must be promptly corrected or removed from my report.

15 U.S.C. 1681i ( d ) Notification of Results CRAs must provide me with the results of the reinvestigation and a revised credit report if any changes are made.

Consumer complaint narrative:
I am filing this complaint to report the failure of financial institution and the involved credit reporting agencies to adequately investigate and resolve disputes regarding unauthorized and unknown accounts and transactions reported to my credit report. This failure violates my rights under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681, and the Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( EFTA ), 15 U.S.C. 1693. 

Specific Issues : 1. Unauthorized Accounts : I have identified multiple accounts placed under my name that I did not open or authorize. Despite submitting disputes with supporting evidence, these accounts remain on my credit report. 
2. Deleted Accounts Reinserted Without Notification : Accounts that were previously deleted after dispute resolution have been reinserted into my credit file without my knowledge or the required notification under 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) ( 5 ) ( B ).

3. Failure to Remove Unauthorized Entries : Several accounts and transactions I reported as unauthorized have not been removed, and the credit reporting agencies have failed to provide adequate explanations or verify the accuracy of the disputed information.

These inaccuracies have caused significant harm to my credit standing and financial well-being. Despite my efforts to resolve these issues through direct communication with the credit reporting agencies and financial institutions involved, I have been met with dismissal and insufficient investigation.

Relevant Laws : 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) ( 5 ) ( B ) : Requires that credit reporting agencies notify consumers within five business days if previously deleted information is reinserted into their credit file. I did not receive any such notice.

15 U.S.C. 1681c-2 : Mandates the blocking or removal of information resulting from identity theft or unauthorized accounts upon receipt of appropriate documentation.

15 U.S.C. 1693f : Provides protections for consumers disputing errors in electronic fund transfers.

This letter is your final notice to rectify your violations. Your failure to comply will be viewed as willful non-compliance with federal law, and I will ensure that the consequences of your negligence are pursued to the fullest extent.

Continuously reporting this charge-off as a new event each month does not reset the statute of limitations and is improper.

I request that you promptly investigate this account and correct the inaccurate information by removing the repeated entries of the charge-off from my payment history.

Please update my credit report accordingly and provide me with a confirmation of these corrections.

These actions violate the following : Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681 : Reporting of impermissible late payment data constitutes a failure to comply with the accuracy and integrity requirements under 1681s-2.

Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692 : Misrepresentation of the nature and status of alleged debts through the inclusion of impermissible late payment data. 
Unauthorized Bankruptcy Reporting : I did not consent to any third-party agencies, companies, or credit reporting entities reporting bankruptcy filings or associated information on my credit report. Reporting this information without my explicit consent constitutes a violation of my privacy and federal laws.

Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681 : Unauthorized reporting of bankruptcy filings is a breach of consumer privacy rights under 1681c, which restricts the inclusion of certain information on credit reports.

Federal Trade Commission Act ( FTCA ), 15 U.S.C. 45 : Dissemination of unauthorized or inaccurate information is deceptive and unfair.

Attached is a letter from the bankruptcy court explicitly stating that they do not report information to any agency, company, or third party. This demonstrates that such reporting is not only unauthorized but also unsubstantiated by the primary source of the alleged data. 

Secure Party Status As a secured party under UCC1 filing number XXXX, I assert all rights and protections available under the Uniform Commercial Code and federal consumer protection laws to safeguard my privacy and financial interests. 

Desired Resolution I demand the following actions : Immediate removal of all late payment entries and bankruptcy reporting from my credit reports. 
A formal investigation into the reporting practices of the entities responsible for these violations. 
Full compliance with federal consumer protection laws, including adherence to FCRA standards for accuracy, privacy, and integrity in credit reporting. 
Financial restitution for the harm caused by these unauthorized and unlawful reporting actions. 
Attachments The following documents are included as supporting evidence : FTC affidavit dated XX/XX/year>, detailing violations of consumer protection laws. 
A letter from the bankruptcy court confirming they do not report information to third parties.

RE : 15 U.S. Code 1681 Congressional Findings and Purpose** ( a ) Accuracy and fairness of credit reporting. Congress has found that : ( 1 ) The banking system depends on accurate and fair credit reporting. Inaccurate reports impair the system 's efficiency, and unfair credit reporting undermines public confidence, which is vital to the banking systems function. After reviewing my consumer reports from XXXX, XXXX, and Experian, I discovered that you have reported this account as both a *charge-off* and *collection. Please note that a debt can not be both a charge-off and a collection simultaneously. A charge-off refers to a debt that has been written off, and the creditor must issue a **Form 1099-C* to the consumer for any canceled debt. How can you legally continue to collect on a debt that has been *canceled? Collecting on a charged-off debt constitutes **tax fraud, and I will be filing a **Form 3949-A* with the IRS. Charge-Off Definition : A charge-off is the write-off of a debt by a creditor without discharging the liability. While it is removed from the creditors books, the debt may still be pursued for payment. Write-Off and Cancellation of Debt : A write-off is a cancellation of debt from the creditors records, but if the debtor is pursued for the written-off amount, it may be construed as evidence of the debts discharge. More details on canceled debt can be found [ here ] ( https : //www.experian.com/blogs/ask-experian/what-happens-with-canceled-debt ). Tax Impact of Canceled Debt : Under IRS rules, canceled debt is generally considered taxable income. If canceled debt exceeds {$600.00}, the creditor must issue a *1099-C* form to the consumer, reflecting the canceled amount. It is crucial that this debt is not reported to any consumer reporting agency. You ( Creditors Name ) have erroneously reported this account as both a charge-off and a collection, violating the *Fair Credit Reporting Act* ( FCRA ), specifically *15 U.S. Code 1681. FCRA Violation : Reporting Inaccurate Information Under **15 U.S. Code 1681e ( b ), any consumer reporting agency must take reasonable steps to ensure the accuracy of the information reported. Your reporting of this debt is incorrect, and such inaccurate information damages my creditworthiness, credit standing, and overall reputation. As a furnisher of information, you are legally required to provide accurate details to credit reporting agencies under **15 U.S. Code 1681s-2. Furnishers Duty Under the FCRA : Under **15 U.S. Code 1681s-2 ( B ), once you have been notified of the inaccuracy, you must correct or delete the information. The IRS defines a charge-off as canceled debt, and therefore, this debt should not be reported to the consumer reporting agencies. Request for Immediate Deletion : I hereby demand the deletion of the following account from my consumer reports : [ XXXX ] ACCOUNT NUMBERXXXX If this violation is not rectified within **15 calendar days* of receipt of this notice, I will pursue legal action under *15 U.S. Code 1681n*, which allows for actual damages, punitive damages, and legal fees for willful noncompliance. Please be clear : I am not asking for verification or validation of this account. I expect the deletion of the inaccurate information. Any response other than deletion of this account will result in further legal action.

Improper Monthly Reporting of Charge-Offs Experian reporting the account as " charge off '' every month, thereby creating the misleading impression that the account has been charged off repeatedly. Under accounting and legal standards, a charge-off is a one-time event. Repeated reporting of this charge-off constitutes inaccurate reporting and violates FCRA Section 623 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) ), which requires furnishers to provide accurate and complete information. This inaccurate reporting is also in violation of FCRA Section XXXX ( b ) ( XXXX XXXX. XXXX ( b ) ), which mandates that furnishers must adopt procedures that ensure the maximum possible accuracy of consumer information. By continuing to report the charge-off on a monthly basis, Experian has fraudulently extended the negative impact of this event on my credit score. Experian Improper Reporting of Credit Limits on Charged-Off Accounts In addition to the above, Experian has also reported a credit limit on the charged-off and closed account. This is misleading because a charged-off account is no longer an active line of credit. Reporting a credit limit falsely suggests that there is still available credit, which affects my credit utilization ratio and further damages my credit score. This practice is in clear violation of the accuracy standards required under 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ), as the information furnished is neither relevant nor accurate. Misleading Reporting of a Balance on a Charged-Off Account Furthermore, Experian continues to report a negative balance on the charged-off accounts they have furnished on my credit report, while also maintaining the status of the account as " charged off. '' This reporting is misleading and suggests that the debt is still tied to the original creditor, even though they no longer own it, having sold it to a third party. Under Rev. Rul. 70-367, 1970-2 C.B. 37, once a bad debt deduction is taken, the debt is considered worthless, and any subsequent attempt to claim ownership or collect on it constitutes an improper attempt at double recovery. XXXX. Violation of Federal Tax Law Principles of Double Recovery This issue also implicates principles established in federal tax law regarding double recovery. Several key cases emphasize that creditors can not claim a bad debt deduction while simultaneously asserting continued : The U.S. Supreme Court ruled that a taxpayer must recognize income when a debt is discharged to prevent benefiting from both a deduction and continued control over the debt. This principle applies here because you can not continue reporting and benefiting from the charge-off while the debt has been discharged or sold. The Tax Court ruled that once a debt is claimed as uncollectible, it can not be treated as still owed. By continuing to report the account, Experian are attempting to assert the existence of a debt that has already been deemed worthless. This case reinforces that a creditor can not claim a bad debt deduction while simultaneously attempting to assert the debts collectibility. ruled that a debt must be proven worthless before a deduction can be claimed, and any subsequent assertion of the debts collectibility would be improper.Please also see myrequesttoopt.

I opened my account with Citibank on XX/XX/2023, and it was abruptly closed in XX/XX/2023 without sufficient explanation or notice. 
2. Citibank representatives claim the account was closed because I refused to pay, which is untrue. I was exercising my right to dispute a payment under the Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ), not refusing to pay. Disputing a payment is a protected right and does not constitute grounds for account closure. 
3. Citibank representatives stated that my account is in collections, even though the account was not in default at the time of closure. This is a misrepresentation of the accounts status and may constitute a violation of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) and Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) if such information was reported to credit bureaus. 
4. The closure of my account while I was disputing a charge appears retaliatory and discriminatory, violating the Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ), which prohibits creditors from taking adverse action against consumers for exercising their rights. 
Relevant Legal Violations : 1. Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ) : Citibanks closure of my account while I was disputing a payment constitutes discrimination and retaliation for exercising my consumer rights under federal law. 
2. Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ) : The FCBA protects consumers who dispute billing errors. Citibank failed to properly address my dispute before closing the account, which violates my rights under this law. 
3. Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) : Citibanks claim that my account is in collections, despite it not being in default, constitutes a violation of the FDCPA, as it is a misrepresentation of the debts status. 
Additionally, I have requested validation of the alleged debt. If Citibank can not validate the debt, they must cease all collection efforts immediately. 
4. Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) : The TILA requires lenders to provide clear and transparent information about credit accounts. Citibank failed to provide adequate notice or explanation for the account closure, potentially violating this law. 
5. Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) : If Citibank has reported my account as delinquent or in collections to credit bureaus, this constitutes a violation of the FCRA because the account was not in default. 
6. Consumer Financial Protection Act ( CFPA ) : Citibanks actionsclosing my account without justification, misrepresenting the accounts status, and failing to address my disputeconstitute unfair, deceptive, or abusive practices ( UDAAPs ), which are prohibited under the CFPA. 
7. New York General Business Law ( GBL ) section 349 : As a resident of New York, I am also protected under GBL section 349, which prohibits deceptive business practices. Citibanks misrepresentation of my accounts status and unjustified closure may violate this state law. 

My Requests : I request that Citibank : 1. Provide a legitimate explanation for the closure of my account. 
2. Produce the original signed contract for my account. 
3. Provide the chain of titles or ownership records for my account to verify its status. 
4. Validate any alleged debt associated with the account. If they can not validate the debt, they must cease and desist all collection activity and remove any inaccurate reporting from my credit file.

Under accounting and legal standards, a charge-off is a one-time event. Repeated reporting of this charge-off constitutes inaccurate reporting and violates FCRA Section 623 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) ), which requires furnishers to provide accurate and complete information. This inaccurate reporting is also in violation of FCRA Section 607 ( b ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) ), which mandates that furnishers must adopt procedures that ensure the maximum possible accuracy of consumer information. By continuing to report the charge-off on a monthly basis, Experian has fraudulently extended the negative impact of this event on my credit score. Experian Improper Reporting of Credit Limits on Charged-Off Accounts In addition to the above, Experian has also reported a credit limit on the charged-off and closed account. This is misleading because a charged-off account is no longer an active line of credit. Reporting a credit limit falsely suggests that there is still available credit, which affects my credit utilization ratio and further damages my credit score. This practice is in clear violation of the accuracy standards required under 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ), as the information furnished is neither relevant nor accurate. Misleading Reporting of a Balance on a Charged-Off Account Furthermore, Experian continues to report a negative balance on the charged-off accounts they have furnished on my credit report, while also maintaining the status of the account as " charged off. This principle applies here because you can not continue reporting and benefiting from the charge-off while the debt has been discharged or sold. The Tax Court ruled that once a debt is claimed as uncollectible, it can not be treated as still owed. By continuing to report the account, Experian are attempting to assert the existence of a debt that has already been deemed worthless. XXXX XXXX. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XX/XX/XXXX Experian XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX Dear XXXX XXXX, I am writing to formally dispute the reporting of the charge-off account associated with XXXX on my credit report. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), specifically 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( Reinvestigation of Disputed Information ), and 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( Responsibilities of Furnishers of Information ), I am entitled to request and receive complete and accurate documentation to verify the accuracy and legality of this accounts reporting. Additionally, under New York law, I am requesting proof of ownership of this debt. 
I would like to highlight several cases that affirm my right to dispute this information and request accurate reporting. In XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX  ), the court emphasized the duty of credit reporting agencies and furnishers to ensure the accuracy of the information reported on consumers ' credit reports. Furthermore, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX ) reinforces the requirement that furnishers conduct proper investigations into disputes and verify the accuracy of their reporting. 
To properly validate this account, I am requesting the following : 1. Authenticated Double-Entry Accounting Records I am requesting full double-entry accounting records for the account mentioned. This should include a detailed breakdown that shows how all transactions were debited and credited, ensuring compliance with standard accounting principles. Please note that I do not wish to receive a simple list of charges or statements. I expect authenticated evidence of the debt. 
The court ruling in XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ) held that mere conclusory statements from debt collectors or creditors do not satisfy the validation requirement. Only authenticated and verified documentation proving the validity of the debt is acceptable.

2. Authenticated Evidence Based on [ Your State ] Law In addition to the accounting records, I require authenticated evidence, in compliance with New York law ( specific code if available ), that you have the legal right to report and collect this debt. This includes original signed contracts or agreements that show my obligation to pay the debt and your legal right to enforce collection and report it to credit bureaus. Without this evidence, the continued reporting of this debt may constitute a violation of both federal and state consumer protection laws. 
In XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX ), the court held that creditors must produce original signed documentation to prove the validity of a debt. Failing to provide this evidence may result in a violation of both state and federal consumer protection laws.

3. 1099-C Form If this debt has been forgiven, canceled, or settled for less than the full balance, I am requesting a copy of the 1099-C form filed with the IRS, which is required if the amount of canceled debt exceeds {$600.00}. If you have not provided this documentation, the debt may be considered discharged, and it should no longer be reported as owed on my credit report.

The IRS has clearly outlined the requirements for filing a 1099-C form under 26 U.S.C. 6050P, which applies when a debt of {$600.00} or more is discharged or forgiven. If you have failed to file this form, the continued reporting of this debt may be fraudulent.

In the absence of the requested documentation and verifiable evidence, I request that you immediately delete this account from my credit report in compliance with the FCRA and New York law. Failure to do so will result in further action, including filing formal complaints with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ), pursuing legal remedies to enforce my rights, and submitting a Suspicious Activity Report ( SAR ) to the IRS for suspicion of fraud. The SAR ( FinCEN Form 111 ) will be filed if you continue reporting inaccurate and unverified information without providing the required documentation. 
Please respond within 30 days of receipt of this letter. I look forward to receiving the required documentation or confirmation that the account has been deleted. 

Thank you, XXXX XXXX. XXXX

Given the circumstances, I strongly believe this account was opened by mistake. XXXX refusal to provide verification raises concerns about transparency and accurate reporting, and it has placed an undue burden on me, both financially and in terms of credit standing. 

Relevant Federal and State Legal Provisions Federal Statutes Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) - Section 611 : Procedures in Case of Disputed Accuracy ( 15 U.S.C. 1681i ) This section requires that inaccuracies on credit reports be investigated within 30 days. If XXXX is unable to verify that I authorized this account, it must be removed from my credit report. I request XXXX ensures correction and removal of this unauthorized account.

FCRA - Section 623 : Responsibilities of Furnishers of Information ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ) Section 623 mandates that data furnishers report only accurate information. Reporting an account that I did not open is a clear breach of this obligation.

Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) - Section 128 ( b ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1638 ) The TILA mandates transparency in loan terms and account openings. Failing to provide documentation that substantiates my authorization for this account contradicts TILA 's requirements for transparency.

Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( EFTA ) - Section 907 ( a ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1693e ) This law requires authorization for electronic fund transfers. If any transactions have been initiated on this account without my consent, it would violate EFTAs protections. 
Consumer Financial Protection Act ( CFPA ) - Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Acts or Practices ( UDAAP ) ( 12 U.S.C. 5531 ) The CFPA prohibits unfair or deceptive practices. XXXX refusal to provide verification for an account opened without my consent meets CFPAs definitions of unfair practices.

Federal Trade Commission Act ( FTC Act ) - Prohibition Against Unfair or Deceptive Acts ( 15 U.S.C. 45 ) The FTC Act allows action against unfair or deceptive financial practices. XXXX lack of transparency and documentation may be considered deceptive.

Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) - Protection Against Abusive Debt Collection ( 15 U.S.C. 1692f ) Although primarily for debt collectors, FDCPA standards on unfair practices also imply that XXXX should provide documentation for any account associated with my name. 
New York State Statutes New York General Business Law 349 - Deceptive Acts and Practices New York prohibits deceptive acts in consumer transactions. XXXX refusal to provide documentation for an account it claims I authorized constitutes deceptive practices, causing undue harm. 
New York General Business Law 601 - Prohibition Against Abusive Collection Practices This law restricts abusive debt handling practices, requiring transparency and valid documentation, which XXXX has failed to provide. 
New York Banking Law 9-f - Consumer Rights Protection for Banking Practices This law mandates fair treatment of New York consumers by financial institutions, ensuring they have access to documentation for any accounts opened under their name. 
New York Financial Services Law - DFS Enforcement Authority ( NY Fin. Serv. Law 404 ) The New York Department of Financial Services ( DFS ) has authority over financial institutions to enforce consumer protection. If my complaint remains unresolved, I am prepared to escalate it to DFS.

New York Personal Privacy Protection Law ( Public Officers Law 91-99 ) This law mandates accuracy in consumer data handling, prohibiting negligent reporting that leads to unauthorized or inaccurate sharing of information. 
New York Uniform Commercial Code ( UCC ) - Article 4A : Funds Transfers The UCC mandates that banks must follow agreed terms for funds transfers, and Fundboxs lack of authorization for this account violates this provision under the New York-adopted UCC standards .

Conclusion XXXX XXXX actions have breached multiple federal and New York State consumer protections. I expect a prompt response within the legally required 30 days, confirming that corrective actions have been completed. Failure to address this complaint satisfactorily will result in escalation to the New York State Department of Financial Services ( DFS ) and, if necessary, further action to protect my rights. 

Thank you for your immediate attention to this serious matter. I look forward to a swift and equitable resolution.

The CFPB found XXXX ignored consumer documents and evidence submitted with disputes, allowed previously deleted inaccuracies to be reinserted into credit reports, provided confusing and conflicting letters to consumers about the results of its investigations, and used flawed software code which led to inaccurate consumer credit scores. The order requires XXXX to comply with federal law, and XXXX must pay a {$15.00} XXXX civil money penalty, which will be deposited into the CFPBs victims relief fund. 

XXXX failed in its basic duty to investigate and resolve consumer disputes about inaccurate information on their credit reports, said CFPB XXXX XXXX XXXX. Todays order requires XXXX to pay a civil penalty and follow federal laws on handling credit reporting disputes. 

XXXX XXXX ( XXXX : XXXX ) is a nationwide consumer reporting agency with headquarters in XXXX, Georgia. XXXX is the parent company to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, and is one of the three major consumer reporting agencies in the United States. It aggregates data about most adult consumers and sells that data to its customers in the form of consumer reports that are used by lenders, employers, landlords, and others to make important decisions about consumers. XXXX processes approximately XXXX disputes each month. 

The Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) requires consumer reporting agencies to investigate the accuracy of disputed information and take steps to ensure consumers credit reports are accurate. For example, consumer reporting agencies must provide notice of a consumer dispute to the furnisher who provided the disputed information, conduct reasonable investigations to determine whether the disputed information is inaccurate, and provide the results of the investigation to the consumer. 

The CFPB found XXXX violated the FCRAs requirements for investigating and processing consumer disputes and assuring maximum possible accuracy of information on its consumer reports. The CFPB also found that XXXX violated the law by using ineffective systems and flawed processes, and excessively deferring to furnishers to address disputes. Specifically, the CFPB found XXXX harmed consumers by : Failing to thoroughly investigate consumer disputes : XXXX process for submitting disputes limits the ability of consumers to fully and accurately describe their disputes. In many cases, XXXX also failed to consider relevant information submitted by consumers, sometimes not looking at the information at all. Then, after XXXX forwarded information about a dispute to a furnisher, it did not meaningfully consider whether the furnishers response made sense, sometimes ignoring information it had that contradicted the furnishers response. Finally, the resulting letters XXXX sent to consumers sometimes contained confusing or contradictory statements, such as both this has been verified as accurate and this item has been deleted. 
Putting previously deleted errors back on credit reports and failing to block identity- theft related information : XXXX did not have systems to detect information that was previously removed and block that information from again appearing on the consumers credit report. In addition, XXXX also had no process to identify situations where a consumer is forced to send another dispute about the same inaccurate information because XXXX failed to correct the information the first time, or because XXXX reported information that had previously been corrected. XXXX policies limited consumers ability to dispute inaccurate information being put on their credit report. Finally, XXXX reported credit information that it should have blocked because the information resulted from identity theft. 
Sharing inaccurate credit scores and data about consumers with lenders : Coding errors in XXXX internal software caused the company to miscalculate and share inaccurate credit scores for several XXXX XXXX consumers. The company also reported the same credit accounts multiple times for more than XXXX consumers. 
Enforcement Action Under the Consumer Financial Protection Act, the CFPB has the authority to take action against institutions violating consumer financial protection laws, including the FCRA, and the prohibitions on unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices under the CFPA. 

The order requires XXXX to : Follow federal law on handling credit reporting data : XXXX must bring its dispute resolution processes into compliance with the FCRA and CFPA.

Consumer complaint narrative: I, XXXX XXXX hereby submit this formal complaint against for violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) in relation to the improper and misleading reporting of a charged-off account on my report Additionally, Experian has engaged in practices that may violate federal tax law principles regarding double recovery, as established in several landmark court decisions and IRS rulings . Improper Monthly Reporting of Charge-Offs Experian reporting the account as " charge off '' every month, thereby creating the misleading impression that the account has been charged off repeatedly. Under accounting and legal standards, a charge-off is a one-time event. Repeated reporting of this charge-off constitutes inaccurate reporting and violates FCRA Section 623 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) ), which requires furnishers to provide accurate and complete information. This inaccurate reporting is also in violation of FCRA Section 607 ( b ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) ), which mandates that furnishers must adopt procedures that ensure the maximum possible accuracy of consumer information. By continuing to report the charge-off on a monthly basis, Experian has fraudulently extended the negative impact of this event on my credit score. Experian Improper Reporting of Credit Limits on Charged-Off Accounts In addition to the above, Experian has also reported a credit limit on the charged-off and closed account. This is misleading because a charged-off account is no longer an active line of credit. Reporting a credit limit falsely suggests that there is still available credit, which affects my credit utilization ratio and further damages my credit score. This practice is in clear violation of the accuracy standards required under 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ), as the information furnished is neither relevant nor accurate. Misleading Reporting of a Balance on a Charged-Off Account Furthermore, Experian continues to report a negative balance on the charged-off accounts they have furnished on my credit report, while also maintaining the status of the account as " charged off. '' This reporting is misleading and suggests that the debt is still tied to the original creditor, even though they no longer own it, having sold it to a third party. Under Rev. Rul. 70-367, 1970-2 C.B. 37, once a bad debt deduction is taken, the debt is considered worthless, and any subsequent attempt to claim ownership or collect on it constitutes an improper attempt at double recovery. XXXX. Violation of Federal Tax Law Principles of Double Recovery This issue also implicates principles established in federal tax law regarding double recovery. Several key cases emphasize that creditors can not claim a bad debt deduction while simultaneously asserting continued : The U.S. Supreme Court ruled that a taxpayer must recognize income when a debt is discharged to prevent benefiting from both a deduction and continued control over the debt. This principle applies here because you can not continue reporting and benefiting from the charge-off while the debt has been discharged or sold. The Tax Court ruled that once a debt is claimed as uncollectible, it can not be treated as still owed. By continuing to report the account, Experian are attempting to assert the existence of a debt that has already been deemed worthless. This case reinforces that a creditor can not claim a bad debt deduction while simultaneously attempting to assert the debts collectibility. ruled that a debt must be proven worthless before a deduction can be claimed, and any subsequent assertion of the debts collectibility would be improper.Please also see myrequesttoopt.

CRAs compile what are called consumer reports, meaning any written, oral, or other communication of any information by a CRA bearing on a consumer 's credit worthiness, credit standing, credit capacity, character, general reputation, personal characteristics, or mode of living. See 1681a.

Federal, state, and municipal law enforcement agencies may obtain basic identifying information ( name, address, former address, employment ) on any consumer through a CRA. See 1681f. If they want more detailed information provided in a consumer report, however, they generally must seek a court order or subpoena. See 1681b ( a ) ( 1 ). 

The USA PATRIOT Act expanded federal agencies access to credit reports. Prior to the Act, the FBI had access to credit reports ( without needing a court order or subpoena ) if there were specific and articulable facts that gave reason to believe that the consumer was either a foreign power, a foreign official, or the agent of a foreign power and was engaged in international terrorism or criminal clandestine intelligence activities. See 15 U.S.C. 1681u ( a ), ( b ). The Act eliminated the requirement of a nexus to a foreign power or its agents and instead requires that the information sought be relevant for various national security investigations to protect against international terrorism or clandestine intelligence activities. See 1681u. The Act also broadened other federal agencies access to consumer reports. Section 1681v obligates CRAs to provide consumer information and reports to a federal agency authorized to conduct investigations of, or intelligence or counterintelligence activities or analysis related to, international terrorism. '' Senior federal agency officials are empowered to issue a certification that the information is necessary for the agencys conduct or such investigation, activity, or analysis. See 1681v ( a ) & ( b ). Upon certification that disclosure to the subject would impair national security or interfere with an investigation, the entity providing the information is not permitted to disclose to the subject or others ( except counsel and those necessary to comply with the request ) that the government agency sought the credit report. See 1681v ( c ). State and local law enforcement within fusion centers often work in conjunction with the FBI or other federal officials to seek consumer reports pursuant to either 1681u or 1681v authority. Consumer complaint narrative: I, XXXX XXXX hereby submit this formal complaint against for violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) in relation to the improper and misleading reporting of a charged-off account on my report Additionally, Experian has engaged in practices that may violate federal tax law principles regarding double recovery, as established in several landmark court decisions and IRS rulings . Improper Monthly Reporting of Charge-Offs Experian reporting the account as " charge off '' every month, thereby creating the misleading impression that the account has been charged off repeatedly. Under accounting and legal standards, a charge-off is a one-time event. Repeated reporting of this charge-off constitutes inaccurate reporting and violates FCRA Section 623 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) ), which requires furnishers to provide accurate and complete information. This inaccurate reporting is also in violation of FCRA Section 607 ( b ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) ), which mandates that furnishers must adopt procedures that ensure the maximum possible accuracy of consumer information. By continuing to report the charge-off on a monthly basis, Experian has fraudulently extended the negative impact of this event on my credit score. Experian Improper Reporting of Credit Limits on Charged-Off Accounts In addition to the above, Experian has also reported a credit limit on the charged-off and closed account. This is misleading because a charged-off account is no longer an active line of credit. Reporting a credit limit falsely suggests that there is still available credit, which affects my credit utilization ratio and further damages my credit score. This practice is in clear violation of the accuracy standards required under 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ), as the information furnished is neither relevant nor accurate. Misleading Reporting of a Balance on a Charged-Off Account Furthermore, Experian continues to report a negative balance on the charged-off accounts they have furnished on my credit report, while also maintaining the status of the account as " charged off. '' This reporting is misleading and suggests that the debt is still tied to the original creditor, even though they no longer own it, having sold it to a third party. Under Rev. Rul. 70-367, 1970-2 C.B. 37, once a bad debt deduction is taken, the debt is considered worthless, and any subsequent attempt to claim ownership or collect on it constitutes an improper attempt at double recovery. XXXX. Violation of Federal Tax Law Principles of Double Recovery This issue also implicates principles established in federal tax law regarding double recovery. Several key cases emphasize that creditors can not claim a bad debt deduction while simultaneously asserting continued : The U.S. Supreme Court ruled that a taxpayer must recognize income when a debt is discharged to prevent benefiting from both a deduction and continued control over the debt. This principle applies here because you can not continue reporting and benefiting from the charge-off while the debt has been discharged or sold. The next morning, XX/XX/year>, I received an email from BofA stating that my account balance was low ( it was now XXXX ). I called XXXX immediately to report the issue with the wire transfer and they said that they would investigate. Right afterward, I also called BofA and told them about the {$1500.00} that I saw the night before on my account page and that had now disappeared. All they said was that there was no activity on my new account. For this reason, they could not help me. I would have to take the issue up with XXXX. On XX/XX/year>, I was reviewing my BofA account when I remembered that they have two routing numbers. I checked to see if I used the correct one for the wire transfer. Indeed, I did not. I chose the one for ordering checks, outgoing payments, and setting up direct deposits. Since that was a Saturday, I waited until Monday, XX/XX/year>, to report this to BofA. They told me that since I used the incorrect routing number, the wire transfer would be rejected and the money would be returned to XXXX. I was advised to wait up to ten days for the matter to resolve itself. I also reported the matter to XXXX hoping that the new information would aid or expedite their investigation. ( a ) Notice requirements Except as otherwise provided in this subchapter, a financial institution may not, directly or through any affiliate, disclose to a nonaffiliated third party any nonpublic personal information, unless such financial institution provides or has provided to the consumer a notice that complies with section 6803 of this title.

( b ) Opt out ( 1 ) In general A financial institution may not disclose nonpublic personal information to a nonaffiliated third party unless ( A ) such financial institution clearly and conspicuously discloses to the consumer, in writing or in electronic form or other form permitted by the regulations prescribed under section 6804 of this title, that such information may be disclosed to such third party ; ( B ) the consumer is given the opportunity, before the time that such information is initially disclosed, to direct that such information not be disclosed to such third party ; and ( C ) the consumer is given an explanation of how the consumer can exercise that nondisclosure option. 15 U.S.C. 1681 is a section of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) that establishes the purpose and findings of the law. The FCRA governs how credit reporting agencies ( CRAs ) access and use consumer credit reports. 
Purpose The FCRA 's purpose is to ensure that CRAs are fair, impartial, and respectful of consumers ' privacy rights. 
The FCRA also aims to promote the accuracy of consumer credit reports, which are essential for the banking system. 
Findings The FCRA finds that inaccurate credit reports can harm the banking system. 
The FCRA finds that unfair credit reporting methods can undermine public confidence. 
Related laws 15 U.S.C. 1681a : Defines rules of construction and terms 15 U.S.C. 1681e : Requires CRAs to have procedures to limit the sharing of consumer reports 15 U.S.C. 1681m : Requires users of consumer reports to disclose the nature of the information to consumers if it's used to deny credit or increase the cost of credit 15 U.S.C. 1681n : Creates a private cause of action for damages caused by willful noncompliance

However, the information remains inaccurate and has not been substantiated with sufficient documentation, constituting multiple violations of the FCRA and TILA. Despite my request for proper verification, the credit bureau has failed to provide proof of verification and has instead chosen to continue reporting incorrect information. 
Violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) : 1.FCRA Section 1681b ( 2 ) - Accuracy of Information : The FCRA Section 1681b ( 2 ) mandates that only accurate information is reported about me. The credit reporting agencys failure to provide proof of verification for these charge-off accounts entry violates my rights to an accurate credit report. Without proof, these charge-off accounts remain incorrectly reported and are damaging my credit.

2-FCRA Section 1681b ( 5 ) - Permissible Purpose : Under Section 1681b ( 5 ) of the FCRA, information in a consumer report must be accurate and used for a permissible purpose. These charge-off accounts are in violation of this section, as there is no valid documentation to support their accuracy or permissibility.

3-FCRA Section 611 - Duty to Investigate : Section 611 of the FCRA requires that a thorough investigation be conducted into any disputed information. Despite my requests, the credit reporting agency failed to properly investigate these charge-off accounts, and as a result, inaccurate information continues to be reported.

4-FCRA Section 1681i - Reinvestigation Failure : Section 1681i requires that, upon dispute, the credit reporting agency must complete a reinvestigation within 30 days and remove inaccurate information if it can not be verified. Your failure to complete a proper reinvestigation and delete these accounts after my dispute constitutes a violation of this section of the FCRA.

5-Failure to Reinvestigate Under FCRA ( 611 ( a ) ( 1 ) ) : Despite providing evidence of inaccuracies in six charge-off accounts, TRANSUNION failed to conduct a proper reinvestigation and left the disputed items on my credit report without adequate verification.

6-Failure to Provide Verification ( 611 ( a ) ( 2 ) & ( 7 ) ) : TRANSUNION did not supply detailed documentation or evidence to substantiate the accuracy of the charge-off accounts, nor did it disclose the method used for verification.

7-Retention of Inaccurate Information ( 611 ( a ) ( 5 ) ( A ) ) : TRANSUNION continues to report inaccurate information despite the lack of verifiable evidence, directly violating its duty to delete unverifiable data.

8-Violation of Privacy Rights ( 604 ) : TRANSUNION unlawfully maintained and disseminated inaccurate information, infringing on my right to privacy and causing reputational harm.

9-Failure to Provide Source and Method of Verification ( 609 ( a ) ( 1 ) ) : TRANSUNION did not furnish the original source of the disputed accounts, or the methods used to verify them when requested, as required by law.

10-FCRA 605B ( 15 U.S.C. 1681c-2 ) : FCRA 605B provides that if any information on a credit report is the result of identity theft or fraudulent transactions, the consumer may request removal of such information by submitting an identity theft report. While this case is not one of identity theft, the section underscores the responsibility of credit reporting agencies to ensure the accuracy and legitimacy of all reported information. TRANSUNIONs failure to verify these accounts violates this standard.

Violations of the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) : Under TILA, creditors are required to provide accurate and timely information regarding loans, charge-offs, and account statuses. The failure to properly report and verify these charge-off accounts under TILA is a clear violation, as the charge-offs should only be reported accurately and substantiated.

I am writing to formally dispute several accounts listed on my credit report that contain significant inaccuracies, which are negatively impacting my credit profile. These accounts violate provisions of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) and my rights as a consumer. Additionally, I have recently become aware of a data breach in which my personal information was compromised. As a result, I do not recognize the activities associated with these accounts, and I believe they may be the result of fraudulent activity. Below, I will detail the specific concerns regarding these accounts, the FCRA laws that are being violated, and relevant court precedents that support my dispute. I respectfully request a thorough investigation and resolution in accordance with federal law, as these inaccuracies not only harm my credit score but also undermine my financial stability. 

The accounts in question are as follows : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( Account XXXX. XXXX, XXXX : {$3800.00} ) XXXX XXXX XXXX ( Account XXXX. XXXX, Balance : {$2800.00} ) XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( Account No. XXXX, Balance : {$4900.00} ) XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( Account No. XXXX, Balance : {$10000.00} ) XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( Account No. XXXX, Balance : {$290.00} ) XXXX XXXX XXXX  XXXX XXXX Account No. XXXX, XXXX : {$2200.00} ) Under the FCRA, consumer reporting agencies are required to ensure the maximum possible accuracy of the information they report. However, the late payments associated with the accounts listed above contain discrepancies in the reporting dates and statuses across different credit bureaus. For instance, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX show conflicting delinquency dates and balances across the various credit bureaus. These inconsistencies are not only misleading but also cause confusion regarding the true state of my credit history, undermining the reliability of the information being provided. The FCRA mandates that all information reported be as accurate as possible, and these discrepancies directly violate the requirements outlined in 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ). Despite my formal disputes, the furnishers have failed to provide concrete documentation that substantiates the late payment entries. According to 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) ( 5 ), if the furnishers fail to provide adequate documentation during the dispute process, the information should be removed from my credit report. Furthermore, these conflicting delinquency dates and balances suggest that the furnishers have not conducted a reasonable investigation to verify the accuracy of the data, violating the FCRAs accuracy standards.

The FCRA requires that when a consumer disputes an account, the credit bureaus and furnishers must conduct a reasonable investigation into the validity of the disputed information. This investigation should include efforts to verify the accuracy of the reported information. In many cases, when accounts can not be properly verified, they must be deleted. The accounts in question fail to meet this standard, as the furnishers have not provided sufficient documentation or proof of the accuracy of the reported late payments. For example, in some instances, the furnishers have not responded to my dispute with any meaningful verification, and the supporting documents they have provided do not conclusively prove that the late payments were valid. As a result, the accounts in question can not be considered verified, and under 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ), they must be removed from my credit report. The failure to adequately investigate and substantiate these inaccuracies constitutes a direct violation of the FCRA.

The FCRA also requires that furnishers of information to credit reporting agencies report accurate and up-to-date information. The late payments reported for these accounts are not in line with my actual payment history and are therefore inaccurate. This failure to report accurate information constitutes a breach of 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ). The inaccurate reporting of these late payments is misleading and harms my creditworthiness by giving the false impression that I have failed to meet my financial obligations. Product: Money transfer, virtual currency, or money service
Consumer complaint narrative:
The short version : Robinhood is illegally preventing its customers from withdrawing funds from their accounts unless they provide facial biometric data they do not have the authority to be collecting. Despite there being many other ways to verify identity, they are refusing to return funds to users who never agreed to using biometric data.

The details : I have had an account with Robinhood since XXXX. In that time, I have only ever linked a single bank account to the account, from which funds were transferred into Robinhood to invest, and occasionally transferred back to when funds were withdrawn. 

6 Months ago, on XX/XX/XXXX, I transferred {$1700.00} from my Robinhood account into my bank account without issue. It was to my surprise, on XX/XX/XXXX, that I attempted to initiate a transfer of {$400.00} from my Robinhood account to the same bank account I've been connected to for over 6 years, and I was met with a prompt to " verify my identity ''. Initially, the prompt asked that I upload a picture of the front and back of my government issued ID, so I took a picture of the front and back of my driver 's license and submitted it. After doing so, I was met with a prompt to scan my face for biometric data. This was a deal-breaker for me. 

I have never in my life consented to giving any company I've done business with any of my biometric data, and I have never consented to giving Robinhood my biometric facial data at any point during my business with them. I contacted customer support to find out how to withdraw the amount without providing this data, as there are plenty of other ways to verify my identity. To my surprise, they refused to assist me, and claimed that I would have to submit " selfies '' ( the app asks for pictures from multiple angles ) to verify my identity to withdraw funds. As a software engineer with extensive knowledge in data collection and, I knew there was no logic to this ask. Robinhood is not in possession of my facial biometric data, and therefore they have no means to use that data to confirm my identity, because they have nothing to compare it against. This was a bald-faced attempt at invasive, unjustified, and unwarranted data collection.

After an extended back-and-forth, the support person, " Deep '', claimed that their customer agreement grants them the authority to withhold my funds from me until I submit facial biometric data. The section of their user agreement they claimed granted them this authority ( section 6, paragraph 2 ) reads : " What this means for you : When you open or apply to open an Account, Robinhood will ask for your name, U.S. residential address, date of birth, social security number, telephone number, citizenship, and other identifying information that will allow Robinhood to identify you. Robinhood may also ask for copies of your drivers license, passport, other unexpired, government-issued identifying documents with a photograph, or other identifying documents. From time to time, Robinhood may ask you to confirm or reverify your identity, or may require that you provide certain additional documents, as necessary. '' When I responded that the paragraph they pointed to did not, in fact, grant them the authority to withhold my funds unless I give them access to my facial biometric data, I explained that what that paragraph granted access to was : - My name - My US Residential address - My social security number - Telephone number - Citizenship - Other identifying information that will allow Robinhood to identify me- Copies of my driver 's license - Passport - Other expired, government-issued identifying documents with a photograph - Other identifying documents.

I explained that I was glad to re-verify my identity using any combination of the above listed articles, but that according to that agreement, no user has agreed to provide Robinhood access to their biometric data. I also questioned why Robinhood insisted on collecting a 3D scan of my face to withdraw funds when : - I was attempting to transfer funds to the only bank account that has ever been connected to my Robinhood account.

- I was willing to provide my SSN, images of my driver 's license, verified transaction history, phone number, email, or any other identifying information available to prove my identity.

- I was able to withdraw over 4 times the amount I was attempting to withdraw 6 months ago.

- I never agreed to allowing them to use my facial biometric data to withdraw funds.

The support person again refused, and this time pointed to paragraph 6, section 3 as the justification, which reads : " You understand that Robinhood may take steps to verify the accuracy of the information you provide to Robinhood relating to your Account in your application or otherwise. You authorize Robinhood or its agents or third-party vendors to contact any person or firm noted therein or in any other information you may provide to Robinhood from time to time, or any other normal sources of debit or credit information and other similar databases, and authorize any such person or entity to furnish such information about you as may be requested or required by Robinhood. You acknowledge that Robinhood may restrict your access to your Account pending such verification. You will provide prompt notification to Robinhood of any changes in the information including your name, address, e- mail address, and telephone number ''.

I then explained that nowhere in that paragraph does the subject of biometric data come up, nor could Robinhood could not possibly use my facial biometric data to verify my identity, as it currently does not possess that information and therefore has nothing to compare newly collected data against, but again was refused and told that I would be required to provide 3D scans of my face to withdraw funds.

Robinhood is now holding my funds hostage and refuses to return my money to me unless I provide them with 3D scans of my face, which I never agreed to, and never will. I suspect this is newly enforced policy they're enacting across all of their users, which means Robinhood is now illegally collecting biometric data that their customers never agreed to provide, and holding their funds hostage if they refuse to do so.

I have an email chain from customer support, screenshots of my account and transaction history, and am willing to provide other necessary information upon request.

Subject : Dispute Regarding Credit Inquiry Made Without Permissible Purpose To Whom It May Concern, I am writing to dispute a credit inquiry made by Discover Financial Services, reflected on my credit report with an inquiry date of XX/XX/XXXX, and a removal date of XX/XX/XXXX. Violation of FCRA 1681b Under the FCRA, a permissible purpose to obtain a consumer report includes : A credit transaction initiated by the consumer. 
A firm offer of credit or insurance. 
The consumer 's written consent. 
A legitimate business need in connection with a transaction initiated by the consumer.

Request for Resolution I request that you : Provide evidence of the permissible purpose that justifies this inquiry, including any written authorization I may have provided. 
Remove the inquiry from my credit report if no such evidence exists. 
Provide written confirmation of the steps you have taken to address this issue. 
Compensate me {$1000.00} for violating my consumer rights under the FCRA, as this unauthorized inquiry has caused harm to my creditworthiness and financial standing. 

Please respond to this letter within 30 days of receipt. All correspondence can be sent to the address listed above. 

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

I am writing to formally request the immediate removal of all outdated addresses from my consumer report, except my current address as stated on my New York State Identification Card, pursuant to my rights under federal law. This request is made in strict accordance with the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681, which mandates the accuracy, relevance, and confidentiality of information reported by consumer reporting agencies. 

Grounds for My Request, As per the FCRA, consumer reporting agencies are required to maintain information that is accurate, complete, and relevant. Reporting outdated addresses that I neither use nor receive mail at, nor list on applications, violates these provisions as these addresses are no longer accurate or relevant. These addresses are both misleading and unnecessary, potentially causing confusion or inaccuracy in my consumer report. 

Furthermore, I exclusively use my current address, as provided on my valid New York State-issued ID, for all official correspondence and applications. I do not reside, receive mail, or conduct transactions from any other addresses. Therefore, the inclusion of these non-current addresses on my consumer report is both inaccurate and unnecessary. By retaining outdated addresses, you are failing to meet the standards outlined by the FCRA for accurate reporting, specifically under Sections 1681i and 1681e ( b ). 

Legal Basis for Removal, Under Section 1681i ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) of the FCRA, I am entitled to dispute the accuracy of any information included in my consumer report, and your agency must promptly investigate and delete any information that can not be verified as accurate and complete. 

Furthermore : 1. FCRA Section 1681c - Restricts the inclusion of obsolete information on a consumer report. 
2. FCRA Section 1681e ( b ) - Requires consumer reporting agencies to follow reasonable procedures to ensure maximum accuracy. 

Outdated addresses are not only obsolete but also introduce potential risk to my identity security, especially if they reflect previous residences or erroneous data. Removing these addresses aligns with your obligation to ensure the report reflects only relevant and accurate data.

Though not an identity theft case, this section emphasizes the importance of ensuring that information reported is verified and accurate, as any unverified or fraudulent entries must be removed.

FCRA Section 607 ( b ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) ) mandates that credit reporting agencies must follow reasonable procedures to ensure maximum possible accuracy in credit reports.

The unauthorized deactivation of my automatic payment ( autopay ) feature, excessive unauthorized monthly deductions, and the inaccurate reporting of missed payments have caused significant financial and credit harm. Background of Issues For several years, I relied on XXXX XXXX  autopay service to ensure timely payments. Without notice, this service was deactivated, leading to missed payment reports despite the bank withdrawing three times the agreed monthly principal. These actions violate key consumer protections and place an undue burden on me, both financially and in terms of credit standing.

Relevant Federal and State Legal Provisions Federal Statutes Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) - Section 611 : Procedures in Case of Disputed Accuracy ( 15 U.S.C. 1681i ) This section requires that inaccuracies on credit reports be investigated within 30 days. If information is unverifiable, it must be removed. I request XXXX XXXX  ensures correction and removal of all inaccurate reports of missed payments in compliance with this provision.

FCRA - Section 623 : Responsibilities of Furnishers of Information ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ) Section 623 mandates that data furnishers report only accurate information. Reporting my account as delinquent despite excessive deductions is a clear breach of this obligation.

Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) - Section 128 ( b ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1638 ) The TILA mandates transparency in loan terms. Turning off autopay without prior notice and making excessive deductions contravenes TILAs transparency requirements. 
Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( EFTA ) - Section 907 ( a ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1693e ) This law requires authorization for electronic fund transfers. XXXXXXXX XXXX unauthorized and excessive deductions without prior notification violate EFTA guidelines.

Consumer Financial Protection Act ( CFPA ) - Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Acts or Practices ( UDAAP ) ( 12 U.S.C. 5531 ) The CFPA prohibits unfair or deceptive practices. XXXX XXXX  actionsunauthorized deductions, deactivation of autopay without notice, and reporting missed paymentsmeet CFPAs definitions of unfair practices.

Federal Trade Commission Act ( FTC Act ) - Prohibition Against Unfair or Deceptive Acts ( 15 U.S.C. 45 ) The FTC Act allows action against unfair or deceptive financial practices. XXXX XXXX  unauthorized actions and lack of transparency may be deemed unfair and deceptive under the FTC Act.

Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) - Protection Against Abusive Debt Collection ( 15 U.S.C. 1692f ) Although primarily aimed at third-party debt collectors, the FDCPAs standards against unfair or excessive debt collection apply as a reference for ethical treatment. Unauthorized excessive deductions and misreported delinquencies can be viewed as abusive practices. 
New York State Statutes New York General Business Law 349 - Deceptive Acts and Practices New York prohibits deceptive acts in consumer transactions. Unauthorized deactivation of autopay, unauthorized deductions, and misreporting constitute deceptive practices, causing undue financial harm.

New York General Business Law 601 - Prohibition Against Abusive Collection Practices This law restricts abusive debt handling practices, protecting consumers from financial harm due to unfair practices, including unauthorized charges and misreporting. 
New York Banking Law 9-f - Consumer Rights Protection for Banking Practices This law mandates fair treatment of New York consumers by financial institutions, ensuring they are notified of key changes to their account. XXXXXXXX XXXX handling of my account contravenes this principle. 
New York Banking XXXX XXXX - Prohibition Against Excessive Charges on Loans and Accounts This law protects against excessive or unjustified charges. XXXX XXXX  unauthorized monthly principal deductions above the agreed amount violate this statute. 
New York Financial Services Law - DFS Enforcement Authority ( NY Fin. Serv. Law 404 ) The New York Department of Financial Services ( DFS ) has authority over financial institutions to enforce consumer protection. If my complaint remains unresolved, I am prepared to escalate it to DFS.

New York Personal Privacy Protection Law ( Public Officers Law 91-99 ) This law requires accuracy in handling consumer data, prohibiting negligent misreporting that leads to unauthorized or inaccurate sharing. XXXX XXXX  misreporting of missed payments violates my rights under this statute. 
New York Uniform Commercial Code ( UCC ) - Article 4A : Funds Transfers The UCC mandates that banks must follow fund transfer agreements, with notice of any changes. The unauthorized deactivation of autopay without notification violates this provision under the New York-adopted UCC standards .

New York State Banking Law 596 - Duty to Act in Good Faith This statute establishes the requirement for financial institutions to conduct their business in good faith and in a manner that does not harm customers. XXXX XXXX  unauthorized actions and lack of transparency in my account management are contrary to this duty. 

XXXX XXXX XXXX  actions have breached multiple federal and New York State consumer protections. I expect a prompt response within the legally required 30 days, confirming that corrective actions have been completed. Failure to address this complaint satisfactorily will result in escalation to the New York State Department of Financial Services ( DFS ) and, if necessary, further action to protect my rights.
